title: What should a full-time household chef proposal include?
body_markdown:
A full-time household chef proposal should define the working schedule, meals and portions, menu planning, grocery responsibilities, kitchen duties, cover arrangements and commercial terms. It should also distinguish dedicated household coverage from scheduled cooking visits. Use this full time household chef proposal checklist to compare the same scope across providers, rather than treating a monthly total as a complete description of the service.


**TL;DR**

- A full time household chef proposal checklist should define hours, meals, groceries, kitchen duties and absence cover.
- myCHEF provides vetted chefs for household cooking and weekly meal preparation in Dubai.
- Compare dedicated coverage with scheduled visits before deciding which household chef arrangement fits your routine.
- Ask for written inclusions and exclusions; a sample menu does not define the full service.


For household cooking enquiries, [contact myCHEF](https://www.mychef.ae/contact) with your routine and the service you need. Explain whether you want meals prepared during scheduled visits or a chef present across defined working hours; those are different briefs.

## What should a full-time household chef proposal include?

**A useful proposal tells you what happens on an ordinary working day—and what happens when that day changes.** The menu matters, but so do school pickups, late meetings, grocery deliveries and access to your kitchen.

Ask each provider to complete the same checklist. Where something is excluded, request a clear explanation of who handles it instead.

| Proposal section | What you need in writing | What needs clarification |
|---|---|---|
| Service model | Dedicated household coverage or scheduled visits | What “full-time” means in this proposal |
| Working schedule | Working days, attendance windows and meal deadlines | Whether shopping sits within attendance hours |
| Household brief | People served, portion expectations and meals covered | Children, visitors and different eating times |
| Menu planning | Who proposes, approves and changes menus | How substitutions are agreed |
| Dietary requirements | Ingredients to avoid and preparation requirements | What the kitchen and chef can accommodate |
| Groceries | Purchasing, approval, payment and receipts | Pantry staples and unused ingredients |
| Kitchen responsibilities | Cooking, washing-up, storage and handover | Duties outside food preparation |
| Staffing and cover | Who cooks and how absences are handled | Replacement arrangements and notice |
| Commercial terms | Included work, exclusions and payment terms | Changes, cancellation and additional work |
| Review process | Named contact and a way to resolve issues | How recurring changes enter the agreement |

Keep the completed checklist alongside the proposal. An answer given in a conversation is useful context; an agreed written scope is what you can refer to when expectations differ.

## Does your household need dedicated coverage or scheduled visits?

Start with the outcome you need, not the job title. A household wanting freshly cooked meals at different times has a different brief from a household wanting prepared meals ready to reheat.

Neither format is automatically better. **Choose the arrangement around when you need the chef present, not simply how often you eat at home.**

| Arrangement | Best for | Main advantage | Main limitation to resolve |
|---|---|---|---|
| Dedicated household coverage | Households needing cooking across defined working hours | A schedule built around agreed household meal times | Attendance boundaries, days off and absence cover need explicit terms |
| Scheduled cooking visits | Households with predictable cooking and preparation needs | Clearly defined visits and tasks | Work outside the booked visits needs separate agreement |
| Weekly meal preparation | Households wanting meals prepared ahead | Cooking can focus on planned portions and storage | Reheating, storage space and menu suitability need planning |

These are comparison categories, not claims about a provider’s current packages. Ask the provider to identify the arrangement being proposed and explain where its boundaries sit.

myCHEF is best suited to Dubai households seeking vetted chefs for home cooking and weekly meal preparation. For a full-time brief, ask myCHEF to confirm whether the proposed arrangement meets your required attendance and responsibilities; do not infer dedicated staffing from a recurring booking.

## How should the proposal define the working schedule?

A schedule should show both attendance and output. “Weekday cooking” does not explain whether breakfast is cooked to order, lunch is left ready or dinner is served before the chef leaves.

Write down your normal meal times and identify which ones require the chef’s presence. Then ask the provider to map preparation, shopping and clearing away around them.

### Attendance and meal deadlines

Distinguish the chef’s arrival time from the time food must be ready. Include access arrangements, preparation time and the final kitchen handover in the discussion.

For a Dubai apartment or villa, explain any building registration, visitor access or delivery arrangements that affect entry. Describe your actual property requirements rather than assuming every building follows the same process.

### Changes to the routine

Ask how the arrangement handles an early breakfast, a late return home or a change to the household’s travel plans. The proposal should explain how to request changes and whether they alter the agreed scope.

A useful test is a hypothetical disrupted day: a meeting runs late and dinner moves. Ask what happens to the prepared food, the chef’s departure and the household handover. This tests the agreement without assuming unlimited flexibility.

## What should menus and dietary requirements cover?

A sample menu shows cooking direction. It does not establish how many meals are included, who approves ingredients or how often the menu changes.

Ask for a menu-planning process that covers:

- **Household preferences:** cuisines, familiar dishes, disliked ingredients and preferred meal styles.
- **Portion expectations:** who eats each meal and whether leftovers are intentional.
- **Different schedules:** meals eaten together versus meals needed at separate times.
- **Dietary requirements:** allergies, intolerances, religious requirements and personal preferences, recorded distinctly.
- **Approval and substitutions:** who signs off the menu and what happens when an ingredient changes.

Be specific about halal requirements and any restrictions on ingredients entering your home. Ask how those requirements are recorded and checked, rather than relying on broad descriptions of a cuisine.

Where an allergy is involved, explain the preparation requirements and discuss shared equipment and ingredients before agreeing the service. A preference for avoiding an ingredient is not the same brief as managing an allergy.

If you provide a nutrition professional’s instructions, ask whether the chef can follow them and how portions will be specified. Do not treat household cooking as a promise of medical outcomes.

## Who should buy groceries and manage the kitchen?

**Shopping, cooking and kitchen management are separate responsibilities until the proposal joins them together.** Ask who checks the cupboards, creates the list, approves substitutions and pays for ingredients.

For each responsibility, record both the owner and the handover. A shopping list is incomplete if nobody knows who approves it; delivered groceries are not a completed task if nobody is responsible for receiving them.

Use this sequence when reviewing the proposal:

1. **Check supplies:** agree who checks existing ingredients and usable storage space.
2. **Approve the list:** identify who approves purchases and substitutions.
3. **Buy ingredients:** confirm purchasing responsibility and the payment process.
4. **Prepare meals:** define which meals are served immediately and which are stored.
5. **Complete handover:** agree labels, instructions, receipts and kitchen condition.


![Household cooking workflow from checking supplies to completing the kitchen handover](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/cff2f505-b7d1-4509-953b-7d3fd531667c/body-8011488705d40e3977bfb904cddf630b.jpg)

*Agree who owns each step before approving the household cooking arrangement.*


For a closer look at purchasing and equipment responsibilities, read the guide to [whether private chefs bring groceries and equipment](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/do-private-chefs-in-dubai-bring-their-own-groceries-and-equipment). Use it to prepare questions, then confirm the answers in your own proposal.

### Define the kitchen handover

Ask whether the scope includes washing cooking equipment, wiping preparation surfaces, putting ingredients away and handling food waste. Specify whether household dishes unrelated to the chef’s work are excluded.

For prepared meals, agree suitable containers, labelling and reheating instructions. Ask for food-specific storage guidance rather than assuming every dish has the same storage requirements.

Also identify any equipment the chef needs you to supply. A proposal should not depend on an oven, appliance or quantity of fridge space that your kitchen does not have.

## Why do household chef proposals vary?

Household chef proposals vary because attendance, cooking output and supporting tasks are not interchangeable. Compare these drivers before comparing the commercial terms:

- **Attendance pattern:** fixed visits and coverage across working hours describe different commitments.
- **Meal requirements:** meals cooked for immediate service differ from meals prepared for later.
- **Household complexity:** different portions, eating times and dietary requirements change the brief.
- **Purchasing duties:** grocery shopping and pantry checks add responsibilities beyond cooking.
- **Kitchen conditions:** available equipment, storage and property access shape the practical plan.
- **Continuity requirements:** absence cover and handover arrangements need their own agreement.

Ask providers to respond to the same household brief. Otherwise, a proposal covering cooking alone sits beside another covering purchasing and kitchen organisation, and the comparison tells you little.

## What staffing and cover arrangements should be written down?

The proposal should identify who is responsible for delivering the service and who you contact about changes. Ask how the proposed chef is selected and how your household brief reaches that person.

Vetting matters, but it does not replace matching the chef to your kitchen, preferred food and daily routine. Request an explanation of the selection process without assuming qualifications or checks that have not been stated.

Then address continuity. Ask what happens if the chef is unavailable, whether a substitute is part of the agreement and how you approve any replacement.

**Do not treat absence cover as included unless the proposal says so.** The same applies to household travel, pauses, changes of address and requests outside the normal schedule.

If the proposal is for direct employment rather than a managed cooking service, establish who is responsible for the employment arrangement. Keep that distinction separate from the menu and seek appropriate advice on the applicable obligations.

## What should the commercial terms make clear?

A household chef proposal should distinguish the service charge from ingredients and any other separately agreed expenses. It should explain what triggers an additional charge and how you approve changes before work is added.

Check the payment schedule, invoicing arrangements, cancellation terms and notice requirements. Ask how unused groceries, household equipment and access items are handled when the arrangement ends.

A single dinner party should not silently expand the recurring household scope. Ask whether entertaining is excluded or separately quoted, even when the same kitchen and chef are involved.

Before accepting, request a revised proposal that incorporates the agreed changes. Keeping amendments in scattered messages makes later review harder than working from one final version.

## How can you compare proposals without missing the gaps?

Mark each checklist item as included, excluded or unresolved. Do not award an unresolved item the same weight as a written commitment.

Next, compare the ordinary week: attendance, meals, groceries and handover. Only then compare exceptions such as visitors, travel and absence cover.

Your final test is simple: could someone else in the household read the proposal and explain what happens tomorrow? If not, request clearer wording before proceeding.

## Related guides

- [How a monthly chef booking becomes a weekly meal plan](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/monthly-chef-booking-to-weekly-meal-plan-workflow)
- [What to clarify about kitchen cleaning after cooking](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/do-private-chefs-in-dubai-clean-the-kitchen-after-cooking)

## FAQ


**What should I check first in a full-time household chef proposal?**

Check the service model and working schedule first. The proposal should distinguish dedicated household coverage from scheduled visits and state when meals must be ready.

**Does a monthly chef booking mean the chef works full-time?**

A monthly booking does not by itself define full-time attendance. Ask for the working days, attendance windows and responsibilities in writing.

**Should groceries be included in a household chef proposal?**

Grocery responsibilities should be included in the written scope, even when ingredients are paid for separately. Confirm who shops, approves substitutions, receives deliveries and keeps receipts.

**How do I include allergies in my household chef brief?**

Record allergies separately from preferences and explain the preparation requirements. Discuss ingredients, shared equipment and what the chef can accommodate before agreeing the service.

**Should a household chef clean the whole kitchen?**

The proposal should define the cleaning responsibilities rather than leave them assumed. Distinguish cleaning after cooking from household dishes, deep cleaning and unrelated domestic work.

**What happens if my regular household chef is unavailable?**

The written cover arrangements determine what happens when your regular chef is unavailable. Ask whether replacement cover is included, how you are notified and how a substitute receives your household brief.

**Can dinner parties be included in a recurring household chef arrangement?**

Dinner parties should be explicitly included or separately agreed. A recurring cooking arrangement does not automatically cover additional guests, service staff or event preparation.

**What should I send when asking for a household chef proposal?**

Send your location, intended start date, household size, meal routine and required attendance. Add dietary requirements, kitchen details and the responsibilities you want the chef to handle.


## Turn your household routine into a clear brief

The most useful attachment is an ordinary household schedule, not an elaborate wish-list menu. Show when people eat, which meals need advance preparation and where your current arrangements fall short.

Send myCHEF your intended start date, Dubai location, household size or guest count, and the service required. Include your preferred working pattern and ask for a proposal that separates confirmed inclusions, exclusions and responsibilities.


**Discuss your household cooking brief**

Share your start date, location, household size and the cooking support you need.

**[Send your brief](https://www.mychef.ae/contact)**
